newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N. chief Annan distressed about Sierra Leone.
newsitem.headline: U.N. chief Annan distressed about Sierra Leone.

text.p: U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan said on Sunday he was "distressed" to learn of the coup in Sierra Leone and said local U.N. staff had been seized and property looted.

"The United Nations and the international community firmly uphold the principle that the will of the people shall be the basis of the authority of governments, and that governments, democratically elected, shall not be overthrown by force," he said in a statement.

Expressing concern about the safety of the civilian population, he said he "strongly condemns taking into custody" Sierra Leonean staff working for the United Nations and the looting of U.N. offices, their vehicles and equipment.

The seized personnel were security staff, a U.N. official said. The world body has a political office plus staff from numerous aid and development agencies. A precise number was not immediately available.
"The United Nations and the international community attach the greatest importance to a democratic order for Sierra Leone," he said.

"The United Nations continues to stand ready to assist the people of Sierra Leone in their quest for a society grounded in democracy, the rule of law, respect for human rights and the pursuit of peace and national reconciliation," he added.
Soldiers in the West African state ousted the civilian government on Sunday and President Ahmad Tejan Kabbah flew into exile in Guinea.
The soldiers broke into the housing compounds of United Nations staff and Lebanese businessmen, looting cars, fuel and household goods.
